title: Why is invoicing software still so bad in 2024?
body: I've tried QuickBooks, FreshBooks, Wave, and several others. They all have the same problems: overcomplicated UI, expensive for basic features, and they make simple tasks like recurring invoices a nightmare. I just want something that lets me send professional invoices without a PhD in accounting. Am I asking too much?
label: pain_point

title: Built a tool that generates invoices from GitHub commits
body: After being frustrated with tracking billable hours, I built a CLI that reads your git commits and generates time-tracked invoices automatically. It parses commit messages for time entries (e.g., 'Fixed bug [2h]') and creates professional PDF invoices. Currently supporting Stripe and PayPal integration. Just launched on Product Hunt!
label: project_launch

title: Idea: Tinder but for finding cofounders
body: Been thinking about this - what if there was an app where you could swipe through potential cofounders based on their skills, past projects, and interests? You'd match if both are interested, then could chat and potentially start something together. The tech community needs better ways to find complementary partners.
label: idea

title: 3 years building my SaaS - here's what I wish I knew
body: Finally hit $10k MRR after 3 years of grinding. Key lessons: 1) Talk to customers before writing code - I wasted 6 months on features nobody wanted. 2) Charge more - I 3x'd my prices and lost only 10% of customers. 3) SEO compounds - my blog posts from year 1 still bring 40% of traffic. 4) Boring businesses work - I'm in compliance software, unsexy but profitable.
label: lesson_learned

title: Anyone else frustrated with Stripe's new UI?
body: They changed the dashboard again and now I can't find half the features I use daily. The new charts are pretty but less functional. It takes 3 more clicks to get to customer details. Why do companies keep 'improving' things that work perfectly fine? This is costing me real time every day.
label: pain_point

title: Show HN: Open source alternative to Calendly
body: Got tired of paying $15/month for basic scheduling features, so I built my own. It's fully open source (MIT license), self-hostable, supports Google Calendar and Office 365, has timezone detection, and includes features like buffer times and availability rules. Already got 500 stars on GitHub in the first week. Check it out at github.com/[username]/freecal
label: project_launch

title: Best laptop for programming in 2024?
body: My MacBook Pro is dying and I need recommendations. Should I get the M3 Pro or wait for M4? Or maybe try a ThinkPad with Linux? Budget is around $3000. Mainly doing web dev and some ML stuff.
label: noise

title: The real cost of using no-code tools for your startup
body: Spent 2 years building on Bubble. Here's the truth: It's great for MVPs but becomes a nightmare at scale. Performance issues, vendor lock-in, and customization limits killed us. We're rebuilding in Next.js now. No-code is a trap for anything beyond validation. The 'time saved' initially costs 10x more later when you need to migrate.
label: lesson_learned

title: Newsletter fatigue is real - need a better way to consume content
body: I subscribe to 20+ newsletters for industry news but my inbox is overwhelming. I miss important emails because of newsletter clutter. Tried filters but still not working. There has to be a better way to aggregate and consume newsletter content without destroying email productivity. Current solutions like Substack reader aren't cutting it.
label: pain_point

title: Launching my Notion to website builder after 6 months of development
body: Finally shipping! It turns any Notion page into a full website with custom domains, SEO optimization, and analytics. Unlike Super or Potion, mine focuses on e-commerce features - you can add buy buttons, integrate with Stripe, and manage inventory directly from Notion. Pricing starts at $9/month. Early bird discount with code LAUNCH50.
label: project_launch

title: Idea: AI that writes your standup updates based on git activity
body: So many devs hate writing daily standups. What if there was a tool that looked at your commits, PRs, and ticket updates, then generated a standup summary automatically? Could integrate with Slack, Teams, etc. Would save everyone 10 minutes daily and ensure nothing gets forgotten.
label: idea

title: Why I shut down my profitable SaaS after 2 years
body: Was making $8k/month but shut it down last week. The stress wasn't worth it. Customer support was eating 30 hours/week, competitors kept copying features, and I had no passion left. Mental health > money. Now consulting and much happier. Not every business needs to be forever. Sometimes it's okay to quit while you're ahead.
label: lesson_learned

title: Looking for beta testers for my new project
body: Hey everyone! Building something cool and need testers. DM me if interested. Can't share details publicly yet but it's in the productivity space. Thanks!
label: noise

title: API documentation is universally terrible
body: Every API I integrate takes hours longer than it should because docs are awful. Examples are outdated, error codes undocumented, and rate limits hidden in random pages. Spent 6 hours debugging Twilio today because their docs showed the wrong endpoint. How is this still a problem in 2024? We need an industry standard for API documentation.
label: pain_point

title: Just crossed $100k ARR - AMA
body: Took 18 months but finally hit this milestone with my design tool SaaS. Happy to answer questions about pricing, marketing, tech stack, whatever. Quick stats: 450 customers, $18 CAC, 5% monthly churn, built with React + Node + PostgreSQL.
label: project_launch

title: Marketplace for buying/selling small SaaS businesses
body: Noticed lots of indie hackers build projects to $1-5k MRR then lose interest. What if there was a marketplace specifically for these micro-acquisitions? Lower fees than MicroAcquire, better vetting than Flippa, and resources for first-time buyers. Could help builders exit and help others skip the 0-1 phase.
label: idea

title: Chrome's memory usage is insane
body: My laptop has 32GB RAM and Chrome is using 18GB with just 20 tabs open. This is ridiculous. Tried Edge and Firefox but they're not much better. How do other devs manage this?
label: noise

title: Failed startup post-mortem: Don't build features, solve problems
body: Burned through $50k and 14 months on my productivity app. Why we failed: Built 30+ features based on assumptions, not user feedback. Focused on cool tech (real-time sync, AI suggestions) instead of core value. Ignored retention metrics until too late (90% churned after 1 month). The graveyard is full of feature-rich products nobody wanted.
label: lesson_learned

title: There's no good solution for email warmup in 2024
body: Starting a new SaaS and need to send transactional emails, but all the major providers require 'warming up' your domain. The warmup services are sketchy, manual warming takes months, and even then you might get blacklisted randomly. Email deliverability is a nightmare that nobody talks about enough. This is blocking so many indie projects.
label: pain_point

title: Show IH: Built a browser extension that blocks all AI content
body: Fed up with AI-generated articles clogging search results, I built a Chrome extension that detects and hides AI content. Uses multiple detection methods (writing patterns, metadata, known AI sites). Also shows a trust score for human-written content. 10k installs in first month! Available free on Chrome store.
label: project_launch

title: Idea: Uber for lawn care
body: Homeowners post their lawn, local teens/contractors bid on jobs. Take a 20% platform fee. Could expand to snow removal, leaf raking, etc. The gig economy hasn't really hit lawn care yet. Thoughts on this? Worth building an MVP?
label: idea

title: Customer support for solo founders - it's killing me
body: I'm drowning in support tickets. Have 200 customers but spending 4 hours daily on support. Can't afford to hire yet. Tried chatbots but customers hate them. Knowledge base doesn't reduce tickets. Other solo founders - how do you handle this? I'm close to burnout and considering shutting down even though revenue is growing.
label: pain_point

title: Anyone going to TechCrunch Disrupt?
body: Got my tickets! Super excited. Let's meetup if you're going. Will be there all three days wearing my startup's t-shirt.
label: noise

title: Don't use AWS for your MVP - learned the hard way
body: Spent 3 months setting up 'proper' infrastructure on AWS for my MVP. Kubernetes, RDS, CloudFront, the works. Bill hit $800/month with zero users. Migrated everything to a $20 VPS on Hetzner, runs better. Over-engineering killed my runway. Start simple, scale when you have customers, not before.
label: lesson_learned

title: Social media scheduling tools all miss this one feature
body: I manage 10+ client accounts and no tool lets me bulk-upload posts with different publish times per account. They all assume one schedule for all accounts. I waste hours every week doing what should be a simple CSV import. Currently using spreadsheets and manual posting. This gap in the market is driving me crazy.
label: pain_point

title: Launched: AI code review tool that actually understands context
body: Traditional linters catch syntax but miss logic bugs. Built a tool that understands your entire codebase context, catches business logic issues, suggests performance improvements, and learns from your team's patterns. Integrates with GitHub/GitLab. Processing 1M+ lines of code daily across 50 teams. Free tier available at codereview.ai
label: project_launch

title: Platform to connect junior devs with real projects
body: Junior devs need experience, startups need affordable help. Platform idea: startups post small, well-scoped tasks, juniors complete them for portfolio+payment, seniors review code for quality. Everyone wins. Could charge startups a platform fee or subscription. Would this solve the junior dev experience problem?
label: idea

title: B2B SaaS idea: Automated vendor onboarding
body: Every company I've worked at has painful vendor onboarding. Collecting tax forms, insurance certificates, banking details - it's all manual emails and spreadsheets. A platform that automates this with smart forms, document verification, and integration with accounting systems could save enterprises massive time. The compliance angle makes it sticky too.
label: idea

title: Killed my startup by chasing perfection
body: 18 months, no launch. Kept refactoring code, adding features, polishing design. Competitors launched similar products and captured the market while I was 'almost ready'. Finally launched to crickets. Perfectionism is procrastination in disguise. Ship garbage and iterate. A launched imperfect product beats a perfect idea every time.
label: lesson_learned

title: WebRTC is still impossibly complex for video calling
body: Trying to add video calls to my app. WebRTC documentation is from 2015, every library is either abandoned or costs $500+/month, and debugging connection issues is impossible. Spent 2 weeks and still can't get it working reliably. Why is real-time video still this hard? Would pay good money for a simple, working solution.
label: pain_point
